display.purpose: Hero headline only. Two lines, capped at 20ch, with a cyan bloom and an amber bloom on the kept half.

headline.purpose: Section openings. Size is deliberately varied band to band so no two consecutive sections open the same way.

title.purpose: The demonstrated document's title inside the history surface.

lead.purpose: The paragraph under every section heading, measured at 34rem.

body.purpose: All remaining prose, notes, and result text.

label.purpose: The only uppercase in the system: Jost at 0.72rem with +0.24em tracking.

brand.purpose: The HESTIA wordmark. Jost 300 at +0.42em, loosened to 0.3em below 620px.

note.purpose: Explanatory notes under a demo: the revert note, the permissions note, the empty-search guidance.

small.purpose: Secondary UI prose: waitlist consent line, revision summaries, the hero scroll link.

fine.purpose: Metadata lines that are read, not scanned: breadcrumbs, revision stamps, result sources, the footer disclosure.

control.purpose: Text typed into or read out of a control. Fixed, never fluid, so inputs do not resize with the viewport.

tree-space.purpose: A space row in the structure tree. Oversized on purpose: this band gives its weight to the tree, not to its heading.

tree-row.purpose: A page row in the structure tree, one step under its space.

headline-close.purpose: The closing band only. The page ends on its largest, centred heading.

headline-loud.purpose: The search band. Opens at the page maximum over a full-bleed field.

headline-quiet.purpose: The structure band. Deliberately demoted so the enlarged tree, not the heading, carries the band.

code.purpose: Actual code only — inline code and code blocks in the document body. Never used to make UI look technical.

shadows.name: control-ignition

shadows.name: field-focus

shadows.name: selected-revision

shadows.name: kept-line

shadows.name: match-bloom

narrative.northStar: The Wake That Never Cools Out
narrative.overview:
The whole world is one image held consistently: a hull crossing a night sea. Everything the sea itself lights — plankton around the hull, plankton under the cursor — burns for a second or two and dies. That is what every other tool does with document history. The wake behind the hull does not die: it spreads, it cools from cyan to amber, and it stays lit all the way back to the top of the document. That is Hestia. The page does not argue this in copy first; it renders it, and the copy names what the reader already saw.

The surface is dark, thin, and quiet. Ground is abyss black (#05070b) with no lighter surface tier anywhere on the page — there are no cards, no panels, no three-column feature grid. Structure comes from hairline rules, left borders, and lit rims rather than from filled boxes. Type is set at ultra-thin weights (250 for headings, 350–400 for prose) at large sizes, so headings read as drawn line rather than as mass. Density is low and vertical: one reading column, left-aligned, in a lane the canvas is deliberately kept out of.

The one deviation the build permits itself is the closing band, which centers after four left-aligned bands so the page ends on a different axis than it ran on. Everything else holds a single left edge.
keyCharacteristics: Two grounds, one vocabulary: paper (default) and the night sea, resolved from the same token names.
Abyss black ground with no elevated surface tier; depth is atmospheric, not stacked.
Two-temperature semantic colour: cyan is now, amber is kept.
Ultra-thin geometric sans (SUIT 250/300/350, Jost 300/400 for Latin labels) at large display sizes.
Controls are dark and defined by a lit rim, never by a coloured slab.
Exactly one authored motion: the fixed-canvas wake. Sections do not animate in.
Authored SVG icons only — 24 grid, 1.25 stroke, round caps, no fills, no glyphs, no emoji.

rules.name: The Two Temperatures Rule
rules.body: Cyan means live, amber means kept, and nothing else may claim either. A cyan element must be something happening right now (focus, selection, a match, the hull). An amber element must be something the product refused to lose (an added line, a past revision, a confirmed registration). Decorative use of either breaks the page's only argument.

rules.name: The No Opacity Dimming Rule
rules.body: Dimmed text is dimmed with a hue-tinted colour at full alpha, never with opacity. A resting search result is #7f9fb6, not foam at 60%. The dimmed states are still body text and still have to clear 4.5:1 against the abyss.

rules.name: The Opaque Base Rule
rules.body: Any control the fixed canvas passes behind gets an opaque base — --control-base for buttons, --field-base for fields. Without it the wake bleeds through and the control reads a different colour at every scroll position. Both tokens resolve per theme, so the rule holds on either ground.

rules.name: The Thin-and-Large Rule
rules.body: Headings get lighter as they get bigger (250 at display, 300 at title, 400 at body). Never bold a heading to add emphasis; move it up the size ramp or change its colour instead.

rules.name: The Different Bar Rule
rules.body: No two consecutive sections open at the same heading size. The heading scale is a rhythm instrument, not a fixed ramp.

rules.name: The Latin Lane Rule
rules.body: Version numbers, dates, paths, and the wordmark are Jost; Korean prose is SUIT. Never set Korean in Jost.

rules.name: The Quiet Column Rule
rules.body: A left-to-right scrim is painted over the canvas every frame — 78%→46%→0% abyss at desktop, 84%→72%→52% below 900px — so the reading column always sits on near-solid black. Text is never placed in the lit lane.

rules.name: The Glow-Not-Shade Rule
rules.body: Every shadow in this system is a light source at a state change. There are no drop shadows, no offset shadows, no ambient occlusion under resting elements. If an element is not doing something, it does not glow.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Borders are 1px and cyan-tinted at 22% (--edge) or 10% (--edge-soft). No thick borders, no double rules, no filled dividers.

rules.name: The Authored Icon Rule
rules.body: Icons are hand-drawn SVG on a 24 grid at 1.25 stroke with round caps and joins, fill: none, coloured by currentColor. Six exist (arrow, lock, search, ring, page, caret). No icon fonts, no emoji, no glyph characters, no third-party icon packages.

rules.name: The One Definition Rule
rules.body: A colour is defined exactly once per theme, in the :root and [data-theme="dark"] blocks of globals.css, and everywhere else it is referenced by name. [data-theme="light"] blocks that restate a value are drift, not theming: the light landing once carried twenty-one such overrides, every one of them a value that had been hardcoded into a base rule and then undone. There is now exactly one light-only rule in the system — the daylight wash, which exists because the canvas is hidden rather than recoloured.

dos: Do reserve wake cyan (#00e5ff) for live state and harbor amber (#f5a83c) for kept history. Ask "is this happening now, or was this held on to?" before assigning either.
Do give any control that sits over the fixed canvas an opaque base (rgba(7,13,22,0.94) / rgba(7,15,28,0.93)); otherwise the wake changes its colour as the page scrolls.
Do dim with a hue-tinted colour at full alpha (#7f9fb6, rgba(125,176,205,0.62)), never with opacity — dimmed body text must still clear 4.5:1 on abyss black.
Do define surfaces with a lit 1px rim or a single edge, and draw structure with hairlines at --edge (22%) or --edge-soft (10%).
Do vary the section heading size band to band (1.5rem floor for structure, 4.6rem ceiling for search) so no two consecutive sections open identically.
Do draw new icons on the 24 grid at 1.25 stroke with round caps, fill: none, and currentColor.
Do label demonstration content as authored where a visitor could mistake it for a real customer — the amber-dotted synthetic note, the finder note, and the footer all say so.
Do run state transitions at 0.4–0.6s on cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1).
donts: Don't add a second authored motion. The fixed canvas wake is the page's only animation; sections have no entrance, reveal, or parallax behaviour, and adding one would compete with the argument the canvas is making.
Don't build cards or a three-column feature grid. There is no elevated surface tier and no repeating tile; the two-column grids that exist are content-specific (rail + document, tree + note).
Don't fill a control with a colour. Buttons are dark surfaces with a lit rim; a coloured slab reads as a different product.
Don't use box-shadow for elevation. Every shadow here is a glow at a state change, and a resting element never glows.
Don't place text in the canvas's lit lane (right 45% at desktop, right 15% below 900px) or weaken the scrim to show more wake.
Don't introduce emoji, icon fonts, glyph characters, or a third-party icon package.
Don't bold a heading for emphasis; heading weight goes down as size goes up (250 display, 300 title).
Don't set Korean prose in Jost, or add a third typeface.
Don't remove :focus-visible outlines or replace the focus glow with a colour change alone.
Don't ship the current demonstration data as real. Every name, date, document, and search sentence in app/data.ts is authored for this page.
